newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds dipped in afternoon trade on Tuesday after an initial slight recovery at the open.
Dealers said guilder debt was likely to fall further after prices slipped for the fourth successive trading day as rate hoke worries linger on.

"The last few trading days investors had been lengthening their portfolio. This gave some support to longer dated debt, but investors start selling this segment as well. That makes the downtrend complete," said one dealer.
He noted some demand in the middle segment, the area between 2002 and 2007, but business was not hectic.

Another dealer said the noted some switching from guilder debt into British gilts and French bonds, but he saw no trend. "It was just an odd trade here or there when a player saw scope for some profit," he said.
Dealers were bearish for the near term as U.S. Treasuries continued their downtrend at the open and dealers did not exclude a rate hike if the dollar jumps further.
The German research institure ifo said today that it could imagine that the Bundesbank would take small steps to send a signal to currency markets if the dollar rose above 1.90 marks.
The dollar was trading at 1.8805/10 mark late on Tuesday.
